old_caption: The video captures a serene landscape featuring a tranquil lake nestled at the base of a rugged mountain range. The mountains, covered in sparse vegetation, display a mix of brown and gray hues, suggesting a dry or alpine environment. The lake's surface is remarkably still, acting like a mirror to reflect the towering peaks and the overcast sky above. The reflection creates a symmetrical image, enhancing the peacefulness of the scene. In the foreground, patches of dry grass and a few evergreen trees add depth and texture to the composition. The overall atmosphere is calm and untouched, with no visible movement or activity, emphasizing the natural beauty and tranquility of the setting. The camera remains stationary throughout the sequence, allowing viewers to fully absorb the stillness and majesty of the landscape.

caption: The video captures a fixed wide landscape view of a rugged brown-and-tan mountain range beneath a flat pale overcast sky, with small snow patches on the upper-left peaks. In the foreground, dark evergreen shrubs cluster at the left while a tuft of dry golden grass lines the bottom edge. A calm lake fills the lower half, mirroring the ridgeline and shoreline as a dark, inverted reflection. Across the excerpt the mountains, shoreline and foreground vegetation keep their positions and the framing stays steady, with no travelling subject crossing the scene. The water surface appears glass-still, so the mirrored slopes and the bright sky patch at the lower right hold their shape rather than being reworked by ripples. The reflection of the tan slopes and the snow-dusted ridgeline remains a coherent, undistorted mirror image throughout. The overall effect is a quiet, undisturbed tableau of the lake and its inverted mountains.

Audit this candidate caption against the actual chronological images, and correct factual errors.
This is a TEMPORALLY CROPPED EXCERPT from a longer video, not a complete event or a loop.
The first view may already be mid-action; the last view need not contain completion. Different
endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

Retain the WISA English narrative style, detail density and paragraph structure. Aim for the
provided original word count within 85%-115%, using genuinely visible details and process.
Do not add repetition, watermark/logo descriptions or atmospheric filler to reach a word count.
Do not shorten a rich caption into a terse technical checklist. Avoid annotation phrases such as
'this mid-segment', 'the excerpt', 'the frame', 'these images', 'observed evidence' in the caption.
This is a direct video description, not an analysis note. No mandatory beginning/end formula.
Complete every sentence. If accuracy requires a substantial length difference, explain it outside
the caption; do not fill missing context by imagination. Optional synonym edits are not needed.

Return JSON {"decision":"keep|edit", "issues":[{"quote":"exact span in candidate caption",
"problem":"concrete visual mismatch or unsupported assertion"}], "caption":"complete final caption",
"length_note":"empty unless required"}. Keep means unchanged caption and no issues. An edit
must actually correct the cited issue. This is a fallible automatic review, not proof of correctness.

draft_caption: The video captures a fixed wide landscape view of a rugged brown-and-tan mountain range beneath a flat pale overcast sky, with small snow patches on the upper-left peaks. In the foreground, dark evergreen shrubs cluster at the left while a tuft of dry golden grass lines the bottom edge. A calm lake fills the lower half, mirroring the ridgeline and shoreline as a dark, inverted reflection. Throughout the excerpt the mountains, shoreline and foreground vegetation hold their positions, with no pan, tilt, zoom or travelling subject. The only perceptible motion is a faint, slow shimmer across the dark water, where subtle ripples slowly rework the texture of the mirrored slopes. This gentle distortion drifts across the reflection without altering the bright tan slope or the snow patches above. The quiet ripple pattern is an ongoing surface movement, drifting steadily rather than marking a new event.
